messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The root cause of the issue lies in the method `BrentSolver.solve(UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)`. When either endpoint `min` or `max` is a root (i.e., the function value at that endpoint is close to zero within `functionValueAccuracy`), the method does detect this by checking `Math.abs(yMin) <= functionValueAccuracy` or `Math.abs(yMax) <= functionValueAccuracy`.

However, the problem is in what the method returns in those cases. Instead of returning the endpoint itself (`min` or `max`), it calls `setResult(yMin, 0)` or `setResult(yMax, 0)`, i.e., it sets the result to the function value at the endpoint rather than the endpoint value (x-coordinate) itself. Thus, the returned root value is the function value (which will be close to zero), rather than the root's x-coordinate.

The `setResult` method stores the passed double into `this.result` without further verification, so if given the function value instead of the x-coordinate, the solver will return an incorrect root.

This explains why the test fails: the test asserts that if the endpoint is the root (`Math.PI`), the returned result should be exactly that endpoint value, but the method instead returns the function value at the endpoint, which is near zero but not equal to `Math.PI`.

There are no indications this is affected by the initial guess logic or bracketing. This is a straightforward bug where the code mixes up x-coordinate and function value in the return for known roots at endpoints.

No relevant hints are found in the recent bug reports, which are unrelated and concern different parts of the system.

Hence, the bug is localized to the early return logic in `BrentSolver.solve(...)` where endpoints are identified as roots, but the return value is incorrectly set to the function value instead of the root coordinate.

Suggested fix: Replace calls to `setResult(yMin, 0)` with `setResult(min, 0)` and `setResult(yMax, 0)` with `setResult(max, 0)` in the code at lines 115 and 127 respectively, so that the actual root estimates returned by the solver correspond to `min` or `max` when those points are roots.

This aligns with the test expectation that the root returned is the root coordinate, not the function value.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
